coverage.non_warrant_content: P001 identifies the equipment turnaround process and four-crew setting as the action scope. The remaining substantive content is captured as claims, with the reported count retained as the premise of the aggregate and temporal-limit claims.

P005 supplies investigation logistics: link six historical weeks of bookings to return, cleaning and collection records by equipment and booking during the two-week investigation, retaining missing values. P006 also instructs agreement on event definitions. P007 specifies comparable prospective recording of those events, expected returns where available, calendar changes and exceptional circumstances. P008 supplies the scheduled-start classification categories. P009 specifies daily review, weekly summaries, the late-bookings/all-bookings rate, delay minutes, stage counts and completeness. These are recording and reporting instructions without an additional stated substantive rationale. The day-14 timing in P012 is retained in the trial-selection claims. Rule conditions, comparison bounds, candidate changes and fallback relations are enumerated separately.

P016 instructs displaying booking denominators and missing-record counts at each time point; it states no separate explanatory conclusion. P018 supplies the material qualification that the candidate patterns are observations to seek rather than findings, retained in the corresponding claim bundles. No candidate pattern is converted into an observed result.

The post-selection ordering in P022 supplies procedural context for continuing measurements and staggering introduction. Its substantive design conditions and all stated conditional inference relations are captured in the claims.

The imperative wording introduces sensitivity checks, advance thresholds and evaluation safeguards. Their substantive bounds and conditional responses are captured as claims; no additional routine setup remains. Undefined measures, thresholds and referents are preserved explicitly in claim scopes.
